results.frozen_answer:
CIS deductions are amounts withheld from payments made to subcontractors in the construction industry, which are then paid to HMRC. These deductions are not necessarily your final tax liability. When you complete your Self Assessment tax return, you will report your total income and expenses, and the CIS deductions will be credited against your overall tax bill. 

If your deductions exceed your tax liability, you may be eligible for a refund. Conversely, if your tax liability is higher than the deductions, you will need to pay the difference. It's important to keep accurate records of your income and deductions for your tax return.

official_sources.rule: Dividend allowance is £500 each year (current GOV.UK).

official_sources.title: High Income Child Benefit Charge
official_sources.rule: High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold is over £60,000 for tax years from 2024-25 (was £50,000 up to 2023-24).

official_sources.title: Who must send a tax return
official_sources.rule: You must send a tax return if self-employed as a sole trader and earned more than £1,000 (before reliefs).

official_sources.title: Tax-free allowances on property and trading income
official_sources.rule: Trading allowance up to £1,000; if annual gross trading income is £1,000 or less you may not need to tell HMRC (with exceptions). If more than £1,000 you can use the allowance as partial relief instead of expenses.
